problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE methods depend on large closed-source VLMs (GPT-4/4o); lightweight open-source VLMs fail on long-horizon navigation because of redundant multi-source inputs, noisy textual memory for progress estimation, and entangled action/stage-transition decisions.
motivation: Lightweight VLMs have limited reasoning capacity, so overloaded single-step inference (panoramas, full instructions, text history) causes attention dilution, hallucinated history and error accumulation. Reducing the inference burden per step through structured prompting could let small open models match much larger ones.
key_idea: Reformulate zero-shot VLN-CE for lightweight VLMs as a stage-structured process over ordered sub-goals, using decision-guided evidence filtering, image-level dual-reference progress grounding, and separate execution and transition inference.
insight: Structuring the inference matters as much as model scale: removing DGMF drops SR from 30.0 to 12.0 and SPL from 20.0 to 6.0 (8B), and removing the transition stage drops SR to 11.0. Removing ISGR raises OSR (45 to 52) but lowers SR (17), so it mainly improves converting proximity into correct stopping. The 4B/8B/32B trend shows the framework is consistent across model scales.
method: DGMF (Decision-guided Multi-Feature Filtering): prompt templates make the VLM fill structured reasoning fields (instruction semantics, VB-STTB analysis, anchor traversal) to filter decision-relevant evidence from views, trajectory and summary before choosing an action; no parameter updates

ISGR (Image-level State Grounding Representation): state = (STTB, VB); STTB holds recent forward-view observations within the current rollout, and VB is a visual baseline refreshed at each sub-goal switch; progress is inferred by image comparison instead of textual memory
SETD instruction decomposition: an instruction is split into ordered, verifiable sub-goals g_1..g_K
SETD execution stage: uses three forward views (-30/0/+30 deg) plus STTB and VB to predict a short-horizon action sequence for the current sub-goal; may emit an early stop on the last sub-goal
SETD transition stage: after each rollout, uses a 6-view panorama (0-300 deg), VB and a rollout summary to output continue/switch; switching on the final sub-goal means task completion
Setup: RGB only, no waypoint predictor, no map, shared Qwen3-VL backbone (4B/8B/32B) with stage-specific prompts

results: With RGB only and no waypoint predictor, LightZeroNav-32B reaches SR 38.0 / OSR 51.0 / SPL 22.0, beating SmartWay (GPT-4o, SR 29.0) and InstructNav (SR 31.0). The 8B model reaches SR 30.0, comparable to GPT-4o-based methods, though SPL (20.0) trails Fast-SmartWay (24.95).
limitations: Evaluated only on a 100-episode subset with high run-to-run variance (e.g. SR ±2-3), and no full-split results
NE and TL are worse than several baselines (8B NE 8.32, TL 18.30), so path efficiency and SPL remain weak
Transition (sub-goal switching) accuracy and failure recovery remain weak; the method relies on hand-designed prompts and many VLM calls per episode
